label: rejected

evidence.V1: Reads instantly as a cut gem from every view: front outline is a clean symmetric crown-over-point diamond, three-quarter silhouette keeps the faceted crown and sharp culet, top shows a crisp octagonal table; A15 X/Y error 0.0.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion split and medium table + 8 crown facets + girdle band read, but there is no small tier (no star/kite facets, no table bevel or sparkle detail), so hierarchy stops at two levels.
evidence.V3: Plain octagonal frustum on an octagonal cone; crown is about as tall as the pavilion and nothing is pushed or exaggerated, so it reads as a correct but stiff primitive gem rather than a confident stylised one.
evidence.V4: Girdle band is the only light-catching break; every facet edge is a razor hard edge with no ~0.045 chamfer, unlike the bevelled rims on the kit anchors, so edge treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown/pavilion, studio and flat) show flat planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or overlap; A18 pass, 0 flipped faces, 0 cap overlaps.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light table, mid crown, dark pavilion), carried cleanly through teal, royal and crimson colourways; disciplined.
evidence.V7: 64 tris against the tiny-class target of 150 (ceiling 300).
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material and one-hue-in-3-values match the kit, but no chamfers and fully faceted shading versus the kit's chamfered, smooth-shaded look make it a minor mismatch beside the anchors.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

evidence.V1: Classic cut-gem outline (wide girdle, tapered crown, pointed pavilion) reads instantly in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view octagon with table also reads as a gem; outline symmetric, A15 X/Y error 0.0, apex centred under the girdle.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion masses and medium table + girdle band are clear, but there is no small tier (no star/kite facets, no sparkle detail), so hierarchy stops at two levels.
evidence.V3: Proportions are a correct but generic octagonal brilliant: tall boxy crown with a large flat table over a short pavilion; reads as a stock primitive gem rather than a pushed, exaggerated stylised shape.
evidence.V4: Facet edges are all razor-sharp with no chamfer; the girdle band acts as the only transition. Facets catch light well (fits a gem), but there is no consistent bevel treatment of the ~0.045 kit kind.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown and pavilion, studio and flat) show clean planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray faceting; gates A17/A18 report 0 self-intersections, 0 cap overlaps, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light table, mid crown, near-black pavilion) with strong value contrast; colourways (crimson, royal) keep the same disciplined three-value scheme.
evidence.V7: 64 tris against a tiny-class target of 150 (ceiling 300); no wasted geometry.
evidence.V8: Uses the kit's single white LF_VertexColor material with one hue in up to 3 values, but has no chamfers at all where the kit uses ~0.045-stud bevels, so it reads slightly harder-edged than kit pieces like the badge.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box collision, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

evidence.V1: Classic crown-over-pavilion gem outline reads at 64 px from front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view is a clear octagon; front outline symmetric, A15 X/Y error 0.0.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion split and a medium girdle band plus 8 crown facets around a flat table, but no small-scale detail (no star/break facets, pavilion is one plain 8-sided cone), so all facets sit at about the same scale.
evidence.V3: Reads as a stylised gem with a chunky crown, but it is close to an octagonal frustum on a cone: the pavilion is a stiff primitive point and the crown-to-pavilion ratio has no exaggeration.
evidence.V4: Facet edges are crisp with no ~0.045 chamfer; only the thin girdle band softens the crown/pavilion break, so edges do not catch a highlight line the way the anchor's bevelled rim and star do.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown, pavilion, studio and flat) show clean planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray triangles; flipped_faces 0, cap_overlaps 0, self_intersections 0.
evidence.V6: A single hue in light/mid/dark values (table light, crown mid, pavilion near-black), and the crimson/royal colourways swap cleanly, so the palette is disciplined.
evidence.V7: 64 tris against a tiny-class target of 150 (ceiling 300).
evidence.V8: Uses the kit's one white material with vertex colours and a hue in 3 values, but has no kit-standard ~0.045 chamfers and is fully faceted rather than smooth with bevels: a minor mismatch.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

top_fixes: Add the kit chamfer (~0.045 studs) on the girdle and table edges so the facets catch a highlight line like the anchors' bevelled rims
Add a small-detail tier: a narrow bevel ring around the table and/or star facets on the crown so the gem has big/medium/small hierarchy
Push the stylisation: lower the crown and deepen the pavilion (or widen the table) so the proportion reads as a deliberate stylised gem rather than a frustum on a cone
Consider a subtle top-light value step on the table (lightest value) vs crown facets to sharpen read at 64 px
Add a small-detail tier: split the crown into star/kite facets or add a bezel/upper-girdle facet row so the gem has a third level of detail and more sparkle variation
Add a narrow ~0.045-stud chamfer on the girdle and table edges to match the kit's edge treatment while keeping facets crisp
Push the proportions: deepen the pavilion slightly and narrow the table so the shape reads more stylised and less like a stock octagonal primitive
Lift the pavilion's darkest value a touch so the lower half does not read as near-black in the front view
Add a small ~0.045-stud chamfer to the girdle and to the table/crown edges so the facet breaks catch a light line and match the kit bevel standard
Add small-scale facets (star facets around the table, a split pavilion with break facets, or a culet tip) to give a third level of detail
Push the stylised proportion further, for example a wider, flatter table with a deeper and slightly tapered pavilion, so it reads less like a frustum on a cone
Lift the pavilion's darkest value slightly so the lower half does not drop to near-black under studio light
